clue.text: Get ready before army chaplain loses heart

indicators.note: to lose the heart is to lose the centre, so the middle letter of the word drops out

parts.note: the prefix meaning earlier or in front
a padre is a military chaplain

explanation.surface: A soldier is told to get ready before the regimental chaplain's nerve fails him.
explanation.walkthrough: A padre is a chaplain in the armed forces; 'loses heart' looks like losing courage but removes the single middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To prepare something is to make it ready in advance, so the verb phrase is a straight synonym.

clue.text: Country fellow each summer primarily wears short underwear

indicators.note: whatever is worn goes around the wearer, so one piece is put on around another
something cut short has lost its end, so the final letter is removed

parts.note: pants are underpants in British usage
EA is the standard abbreviation for each

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of summer

explanation.surface: A rustic man wears skimpy underwear every summer.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain pants means underpants, not trousers; 'short' trims the garment before it goes around the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A peasant is a farm labourer or smallholder living in the countryside, a rural man of humble standing.

clue.text: Describe me? Not married, cross and bald

indicators.note: not married means without the abbreviation for married, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: taken as written
a cross is drawn as an X
a bald statement is a plain, unadorned one

explanation.surface: Someone invites a description of themselves: unmarried, irritable and hairless.
explanation.walkthrough: M is the abbreviation for married, so ME without it leaves E. 'Bald' here means blunt or unvarnished, not hairless.
explanation.definitionFit: To explain something is to set it out clearly in words, which is close to describing or accounting for it.

clue.text: A sketch picked up prize

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting something up makes it read from bottom to top

parts.note: to sketch is to draw

explanation.surface: A drawing collected a prize at an art show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' suggests collecting, but in a down clue it turns the word upward.
explanation.definitionFit: An award is a prize given in recognition of achievement, so the nouns are direct synonyms.

clue.text: All-important titanium and aluminium found south of German city

indicators.note: in a down clue, being south of something means coming below it, so these pieces follow the other one

parts.note: Essen is a city in the Ruhr
Ti is the chemical symbol for titanium
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: Crucial metals are discovered to the south of an industrial German city.
explanation.walkthrough: Two chemical symbols sit below the city name in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Something essential is absolutely necessary, of the greatest importance, matching the hyphenated adjective.

clue.text: Exclamation of disgust about writer's chances

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the word faces the other way

parts.note: pah is a scornful interjection
a pen is a writer, and the apostrophe-s gives the S

explanation.surface: Someone snorts in disgust at an author's prospects of success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chances' looks like a noun meaning prospects, but it is a verb: it so chances that...
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to chance means to occur by accident, which is what happens means.

clue.text: Work inside the man had planned

indicators.note: inside places one item within the walls of another

parts.note: he'd is the contraction of he had
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A worker on the inside had planned the job, like a heist.
explanation.walkthrough: OP is short for opus, the Latin word used for a numbered musical work.
explanation.definitionFit: To have hoped to do something is to have intended or aimed at it, a loose synonym for planned.

clue.text: Parking hotel guest's Ford?

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
a hotel resident is a guest staying there

explanation.surface: A hotel valet parks a guest's Ford car.
explanation.walkthrough: Ford reads as a car make, but it is Gerald Ford; the apostrophe-s is 'is', and the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerald Ford was the 38th US president, so he is one example of the office holder.

clue.text: Numerous sand eels at sea adult avoided

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters get jumbled
something avoided is kept out, so that letter is left out of the mix

parts.note: taken as written
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: Countless sand eels swim in the sea while a grown-up keeps clear.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one A from the two words, then rearrange the remaining seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something endless seems to have no limit, so loosely it describes things too many to count.

clue.text: What horse was, possibly — small and confused

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
addled means muddled or confused

explanation.surface: A little horse appears dazed and confused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confused' looks like an anagram signal but simply gives a synonym; the definition is a whole descriptive phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse fitted with a seat for riding has been saddled, which is why 'possibly' hedges the description.

clue.text: Seems dad rejected fruit

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word is turned backwards

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
pears are fruit

explanation.surface: It looks as though father turned down the fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the short word for dad is turned round; the fruit stays as written.
explanation.definitionFit: To appear is to give an impression of being something, an exact synonym for seems.

clue.text: Be in charge of following page, editor begged

indicators.note: following means coming after, so one piece is placed behind the other

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for page
to lead is to be in charge of
ED is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor pleaded to be put in charge of the next page.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's opening phrase comes after the page letter in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To plead is to ask earnestly or implore, so the past tenses are synonyms.

clue.text: A group one daughter deserted

parts.note: taken as written
a band is a group, of musicians or people
taken as written
D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A band's member, someone's daughter, walked out on the group.
explanation.walkthrough: Four short pieces simply line up in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoned and deserted both describe someone or something left behind and forsaken.

clue.text: Perfect goal — Pele's third

parts.note: an idea can be an aim or goal, as in 'the idea is to win'

indicators.note: third points to one letter by its position in the word

parts.note: the third letter of the footballer's name

explanation.surface: Pelé's third goal in a match was a perfect strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goal' suggests football, but here it means aim or purpose; Pelé was the Brazilian football great.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal as an adjective means flawless or exactly as one would wish, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Pale brown energy drink

parts.note: tan is a light yellowish-brown
go means vigour or energy

explanation.surface: A light brown energy drink is on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Energy drink' reads as one item but splits; Tango is a British brand of fizzy orange soft drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Tango is a branded fizzy soft drink sold in Britain, so it is an example of a drink.

clue.text: So is Cognac unfortunately no good for social events?

indicators.note: something going unfortunately has gone wrong, so the letters are put out of order
no good means without the abbreviation for good, so that letter is struck out

parts.note: taken as written
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether brandy is sadly unsuitable for parties.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip the G from the three words, then rearrange the nine letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: An occasion is a special event or celebration, such as a wedding or party, so the plurals match.

clue.text: Moved one mile then flattened

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
M is the abbreviation for mile
to press something is to flatten it

explanation.surface: A road crew shifted something a mile, then rolled it flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moved' reads as physical movement, but it is emotional: touched or affected.
explanation.definitionFit: To be moved is to be stirred emotionally, and being impressed is a strong favourable reaction.

clue.text: Had gangs used university's shed?

parts.note: a posse is a band of people, a gang

indicators.note: something shed is cast off, so that letter falls away

parts.note: taken as written
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether gangs took over a college outbuilding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like a noun for a hut, but it is a verb; the apostrophe-s is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To have something is to own it, and possessed is the past tense meaning owned or held.

clue.text: Guys from Idaho I caught breaking rules

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so these letters go within

parts.note: taken as written
ID is the postal abbreviation for Idaho
taken as written
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Men from Idaho say they were caught breaking the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guys' reads as men, but it is a verb: to guy someone is to mock them.
explanation.definitionFit: To guy is an old verb for making fun of a person, so guys and ridicules are equivalent.

clue.text: Rumours about pet turning up

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up makes a word read from the bottom upward

parts.note: a pet is a fit of sulking, as is a strop

explanation.surface: Gossip spreads about a lost pet that reappeared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' reads as an animal, but it means a sulk, as in 'in a pet'; a strop is British slang for a bad temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Reports can be accounts that are passed around unconfirmed, much like rumours or hearsay.

clue.text: Put down spades I discovered in storehouse

indicators.note: something discovered in a place is found within it, so these letters sit inside

parts.note: a depot is a warehouse
S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone found spades hidden in a warehouse and set them down.
explanation.walkthrough: The two short pieces go inside the storehouse word between its O and T.
explanation.definitionFit: To deposit something is to lay it down or place it somewhere, matching put down.

clue.text: River boat initially stuck in bank

indicators.note: something stuck in another is lodged inside it

parts.note: a bank is a row or tier, as of seats or oars

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of boat

explanation.surface: A river boat runs aground at first on the riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' reads as a riverbank, but it means a row, as in a bank of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tiber is the river flowing through Rome, so it is a specific instance of a river.

clue.text: Black bird first to leave fence

indicators.note: the first letter leaving means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a harrier is a bird of prey

explanation.surface: A dark bird is the first to fly off a fence.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird loses its H, leaving ARRIER to follow B.
explanation.definitionFit: A fence is a structure that blocks passage, which is exactly what a barrier does.

clue.text: Cryptic puzzles idlers do almost cracked

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
cracked means broken apart, so the letters are reassembled differently

parts.note: taken as written
do with its last letter gone

explanation.surface: Lazy people nearly solve the crosswords they attempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracked' looks like solved, the natural partner of puzzles, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle is a puzzling question with a hidden or punning answer, a classic kind of cryptic puzzle.

clue.text: Fizzy drinks enthralling eastern religious leaders

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: pop is a fizzy soft drink
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: Sparkling drinks delight priests from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enthralling' reads as captivating, but it signals holding letters inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A pope is the head of the Roman Catholic Church, so popes are religious leaders.

clue.text: Change the elders kept safe

indicators.note: to change something is to alter its form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Coins given as change were kept safe by the old folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' looks like a noun for coins, but it is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To shelter someone is to protect them from harm or weather, so sheltered means protected.

clue.text: Disreputable tennis player maybe touching lady's rear

parts.note: a seed is a ranked player in a tennis draw

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its tail end, so only the last letter is taken

parts.note: the final letter of lady

explanation.surface: A shady tennis player puts a hand on a woman's bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touching' here means next to, joining the two pieces end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: Seedy describes something sleazy or squalid, of doubtful respectability.

clue.text: The Beano's regularly chosen for adolescents

indicators.note: picking at regular intervals means every other letter is taken

parts.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters of these words

explanation.surface: The Beano comic is often picked by young readers.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters; The Beano is a long-running British children's comic.
explanation.definitionFit: Teens is informal for teenagers, young people between childhood and adulthood.

clue.text: Empty rifle shop put back

indicators.note: an emptied word has lost its contents, leaving just the outside letters

parts.note: the outside letters of rifle
a store is a shop

explanation.surface: Someone has cleaned out a gun shop and must return the stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rifle' could be the verb meaning ransack, but here it is the gun, hollowed out.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore something is to return it to its original place or owner, so it means to put back.

clue.text: Place is awfully significant

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly, so the letters come out in a mess

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A location is said to be terribly important.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' reads as an intensifier meaning very, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something special stands out as important or noteworthy, close to significant.

clue.text: Meet perhaps without heads of the international sales force

indicators.note: without can mean outside, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: say is used to mean for example or perhaps

indicators.note: the heads of words are their opening letters

parts.note: the opening letters of four words

explanation.surface: A sales conference might go ahead without the leaders of the global team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like lacking, but it means outside: SAY goes around the four initials.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet a demand or requirement is to fulfil it, which is what satisfy means.

clue.text: Among nudes, I restrained longings

indicators.note: among means in the midst of, so the letters sit within the phrase

parts.note: the letters run on from the end of the first word through to the start of the last

explanation.surface: Someone surrounded by naked figures held their urges in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Restrained' sounds like self-control, but it is padding around the hidden letters; the punctuation and spaces are ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Desires are strong wishes or cravings, the same as longings.
